# ARTEX **Autonomous penetration testing that keeps its receipts.** (upstream: [Autumn-27/ARTEX](https://github.com/Autumn-27), AGPL-3.0) Self-hosted multi-agent offensive security. A planner explores, workers run real tools, and every finding stays bound to the assets and HTTP traffic that prove it. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/BaaRai/ARTEX?label=release&color=6b34db)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](LICENSE) [![CI](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Go](https://img.shields.io/github/go-mod/go-version/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](go.mod) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#installation) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Security](SECURITY.md)
--- ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration testing platform. It is not a chat wrapper around a scanner: a planner splits a goal into intents, workers execute them with real tools, and the results are written back into **two linked graphs**: one for what you know about the target, one for how the test is progressing. Every finding can carry the captured request and response that justify it, and every autonomous action passes through scope rules, approval gates and budgets. - **It explores, it doesn't chat.** Goal decomposition, intent dispatch, worker execution and write-back form a closed loop that keeps advancing until the goal is proven. - **Two graphs, one audit trail.** The shared asset graph says *what exists*; the per-task exploration graph says *what was tried, what it produced, and why*. Anchors link the two. - **Findings with evidence.** A recording MITM proxy and a browser extension capture real traffic; findings, evidence quotes and retests are tied to the exact request/response. - **Autonomy with brakes.** Human-in-the-loop approvals, argv-prefix rules, scope/deny gates, token and turn budgets, a target noise governor, and prompt-injection framing on tool output. - **Self-hosted and model-agnostic.** One Go binary with the Next.js UI embedded, PostgreSQL, your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama. --- ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and optionally an LLM key) docker compose up -d --build # builds from this checkout, starts PostgreSQL ``` Open **http://localhost:8787**. On the first visit `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token printed at startup: ```bash docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token" ``` > Multi-arch release images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) are published to GitHub Container > Registry at `ghcr.io/baarai/artex` from the next tagged release; v0.7.0 predates the publish > step. For pulling the prebuilt image and all other installation paths (script, binaries, > source, release archives), see [Installation](#installation). --- ## Multi-provider workers In **System → LLM**, configure the profiles you want to use. In **System → Settings**, set the concurrent worker count to at least **2** before starting a task (the count applies to subsequently started tasks). In **System → Agents → Worker**, leave the model set to follow the task; a fixed Worker model takes precedence over rotation. When creating a task, select both profiles in **LLM config chain**, arrange their order, and enable **Enable multi-LLM worker rotation**. For an existing task, open its LLM config control, change the switch or profile order, and save. Rotation assigns successive worker intents A, B, A, B, regardless of completion order. Separate intents can run concurrently on different providers; each intent keeps its selected provider unless it fails over. Planner and other unbound roles continue using the task's current profile. Turning rotation off restores ordered task-level failover. An excluded provider is skipped, so an intent pinned to an exhausted profile falls back to the task's current profile instead of retrying it; rotation keeps cycling the whole list and does not rebalance around a dead provider. Saving the chain resets their failure state. Changes do not interrupt in-flight calls. The rotation cursor starts again after a server restart and saving the chain does not reset it; the profile order and switch remain persisted. The task creation and `PUT /api/tasks/{id}/llm` APIs accept `llm_rotate: true` alongside the ordered `llm_profile_ids`. Omitting `llm_rotate` on an update preserves its value. ## Screenshots | Tasks | Findings | | :---: | :---: | | ![Tasks](screenshots/tasks.png) | ![Findings](screenshots/findings.png) | | Task execution: sessions and tool calls | Exploration graph | | :---: | :---: | | ![Execution](screenshots/sessions.png) | ![Exploration graph](screenshots/graph.png) | | Asset coverage graph | Traffic recording | | :---: | :---: | | ![Asset coverage graph](screenshots/assets_test.png) | ![Traffic](screenshots/traffic.png) | | Human-in-the-loop chat | Interception approvals | | :---: | :---: | | ![Chat](screenshots/chat.png) | ![Interception](screenshots/intercept.png) |
More screenshots (assets, agents, LLM, logs) | Assets | Agent management | | :---: | :---: | | ![Assets](screenshots/assets.png) | ![Agent](screenshots/agents.png) | | LLM configuration | Backend logs | | :---: | :---: | | ![LLM](screenshots/llm.png) | ![Logs](screenshots/logs.png) |
--- ## How it works ### Dual-graph architecture: exploration graph + asset graph ARTEX separates *what the goals are* from *how far testing has progressed* into two independent graphs linked by anchors: - **Asset graph (shared across tasks).** One source of truth for `root_domain / subdomain / ip / service / app / endpoint`, owned by companies. Parent-child relationships and deduplication keys are computed by the program; agents only submit raw observations. - **Exploration graph (per task).** The task's reasoning and progress: `goal / intent / fact / finding / hint` nodes connected by `spawns / derived_from / yields / proves` edges into a lineage chain. - **Anchors link them.** `exploration_anchors(node_id, asset_id)` ties intents, facts and findings to concrete assets: which assets a direction touched, and which intents tested a given asset. This also powers **asset test coverage** and the coverage graph. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph EG["Exploration graph (per-task · advance chain)"] direction TB G["goal"] I1["intent A"] F1["fact"] I2["intent B"] FD["finding (vulnerability)"] G -->|spawns| I1 I1 -->|yields| F1 F1 -->|derived_from| I2 I2 -->|proves| FD end subgraph AG["Asset graph (globally shared · source of truth)"] direction TB RD["root_domain"] SD["subdomain"] SV["service"] EP["endpoint"] RD --> SD --> SV --> EP end I1 -. anchor .-> SD F1 -. anchor .-> SV I2 -. anchor .-> EP FD -. anchor .-> EP ``` The **planner** reads the exploration graph, judges goals, and dispatches intents only when there is an uncovered direction; a **worker** claims one intent, executes it, writes assets/facts/findings back into both graphs, then stops. ### The engine loop The engine is event-driven: any graph change wakes the planner, workers claim and execute intents, write-back triggers the next round, until `prove_goal` closes the task. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant EV as graph-change debounce participant P as planner participant FR as frontier intent queue participant W as worker participant PX as recording proxy participant DB as dual graphs + activity EV-->>P: wake up P->>DB: read situation (graph_overview prefetch + coverage/scope) P->>FR: dispatch 0..N intents (with asset_ids) Note over P,FR: most wake-ups dispatch 0 (no new direction means done) W->>FR: claimNext claims one intent W->>DB: fetch the raw assets of the intent's asset_ids W->>PX: real tool execution (Kali / Bash / HTTP) PX-->>W: response (fully traced + CA verified) W->>DB: write back fact / asset / finding + per-step activity DB-->>EV: graph change EV-->>P: wake again (closed loop) ``` ### Durable attack chains, shared worker memory Real attack chains are multi-step and ordered (find an injection → get credentials → move laterally). The planner keeps a **todolist retained per task across wake-ups**: it records the chain once, then dispatches the next step only when its prerequisites are satisfied by facts. Workers can also **search each other's execution traces** (`search_all_worker_traces`, `list_worker_traces`, `get_worker_trace`). Observations that never became formal facts (an error message, a response snippet, a hidden parameter) are still reusable by the next worker, while each worker remains confined to the intent it claimed. --- ## Features ### Evidence, not chat logs - **Recording MITM proxy** (`:8788`) with a generated CA: every Bash/HTTP tool call is traced, and request/response evidence can be bound to a finding. - **Browser extension** (`extension/`) for authenticated targets: log in once (captcha, email OTP, 2FA included), capture the session, and the requests/responses land in the same traffic store.
Using the traffic capture extension - Load the unpacked extension from `extension/` (Chrome/Edge: Developer Mode → Load unpacked); - In the popup, set your ARTEX URL and token, then press **Start capture** on the tab you are browsing; - Use the site normally; text requests/responses are batched to `POST /api/traffic/ingest` (authenticated). Binary bodies (images, fonts) are skipped, bodies are truncated at 256 KiB, batches are capped at 50 entries; - Press **Stop** when done. Everything stays in your local traffic store.
- **Verified findings**: findings carry a POE level, a verification status and a note; a finding is `verified` only when a bound proof/response and verbatim evidence quotes support it. Gzip/deflate bodies are decoded before the quote check. The findings table supports bulk status updates, and the report and export show each finding's proof strength next to its status. - **Traffic replay**: open a captured exchange and replay the recorded request (method, URL, headers and stored body) from the traffic detail; replay stays disabled while only the body preview is loaded. - **Vulnerability retest loop**: a dedicated `retester` agent re-runs a finding with optional fixed version/conditions, records `Still reproducible / Fixed / Cannot confirm`, and can move the finding to `Fixed` automatically. Original evidence and reports are preserved. - **Reports and exports**: findings, evidence and task archives, with traffic snapshots kept encrypted at rest. ### Control without slowing down - **Interception gate**: every tool call can require human approval, with rules by `string`, `regex` or **argv prefix**. An argv rule is a JSON array of 1 to 8 tokens (Bash only, for example `["git","push"]`); it matches only a single simple command whose parsed prefix equals the pattern exactly. Pipes, lists, redirections, prefix assignments, subshells, background jobs, wrapper programs and command/parameter substitutions do not match; flags are ignored by construction (`["git","push"]` covers `git push --force`, but `git -C /repo push` matches nothing). Each approval records who decided: `human`, `rule`, `model` or `system`. - **Scope and target gate**: scope rows define the coverage denominator; assets outside the declared scope are not explored. The target gate (off by default, API-only) can refuse destinations that were not approved. - **Budgets**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a whole task (planner and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Near the limit the task enters a forced wrap-up; a worker is not started when the remaining budget cannot cover it. Spend already in `llm_usage` is restored after a restart. A task that is already inside the wrap-up reserve only has that reserve left, so the revived run wraps up instead of starting another worker. The per-worker cost estimate starts again from the defaults (50,000 tokens and 10 turns) until a worker finishes in this process. - **Noise governor**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE=quiet|balanced|aggressive` paces requests ARTEX sends to targets (per-host rate, burst, in-flight limit, jitter, backoff on 429/503, short GET caching). With a profile set, agents also receive low-and-slow flags for the installed scanners. - **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Disable with `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0`. ### Assets and coverage - **Coverage ledger and force-directed coverage graph**: in-scope assets are highlighted as tested or untested, with linked intents, facts and findings per node. - **Company-scoped asset graph**: shared across tasks, deduplicated by the program, with domain → subdomain → service → endpoint containment. - **ScopeSentry sync**: pull asset data from a [ScopeSentry](https://github.com/Autumn-27/ScopeSentry) instance by project or task, merged by company scope into the asset graph for agents to explore.
Syncing from ScopeSentry - On the **Asset Sync** page, enter the ScopeSentry address and API key; - Choose the targets and asset types by **project** or **task** (domains / subdomains / IPs / ports / sites / endpoints…); - Import: rows are merged by company asset scope and become part of the asset graph.
- **Task categories, templates, relations and archives** for repeatable engagements. ### Platform - **LLM profiles with failover**: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible relays and keyless Ollama; multiple profiles per task with automatic failover. - **Token accounting**: per-task and per-session usage, cache reads/writes, and an LLM record view for every call. - **MCP servers, skills, memory and a workspace**: extend the agent with remote tools and reusable prompt/playbook material. - **Web search**: the agent's search tool uses Brave, Tavily or the opt-in Keenable backend, configured in **System → Settings** with the key encrypted at rest; search can also egress through its own proxy. - **Single binary**: the Next.js UI is embedded with `go:embed`; PostgreSQL is the only external dependency. --- ## Installation > Requires **PostgreSQL**; exploration requires an **LLM** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or > `OPENAI_API_KEY`, also configurable in the UI). ### Option 1: one-click install script (recommended) ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX ./install.sh ``` The script detects or installs Docker, then offers **① all-Docker** (writes `.env`, runs `docker compose up -d --build`) or **② local build and run** (generates `config.json`, builds the embedded binary, starts it). Open **http://localhost:8787**; `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token printed at startup (`docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token"`). The UI listens on `127.0.0.1` by default. To reach it from another machine (or from Windows when ARTEX runs inside WSL), set `ARTEX_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0` in `.env` (the setup token still protects the first-run claim), or keep loopback and use a reverse proxy or SSH tunnel. ### Option 2: Docker (Compose checkout build or prebuilt GHCR image) Build from a checkout with Docker Compose: ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, optionally ANTHROPIC_API_KEY docker compose up -d --build # → http://localhost:8787 ``` The release workflow publishes a multi-arch image (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) to GitHub Container Registry on each `v*` tag, with tags `:latest`, `:v`, and `:`. v0.7.0 predates that step, so there is no `artex` package yet: until the next tagged release, use the checkout build above, and `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` and the `docker pull` below will fail with `denied`. GHCR packages start private; after the first publish the package visibility must be set to Public, and the release workflow verifies that the image pulls anonymously and fails the job otherwise. Once the image is published, the standalone container requires an existing PostgreSQL database reachable from the container. Set the `ARTEX_PG_*` variables below. The example uses Docker Desktop's `host.docker.internal` to reach PostgreSQL on the host. On native Linux Docker Engine, add `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` to `docker run` for a host database, or use the reachable hostname of your database server. ```bash docker pull ghcr.io/baarai/artex:latest mkdir -p data keys docker run -d --name artex \ --security-opt no-new-privileges:true \ -p 127.0.0.1:8787:8787 \ -p 127.0.0.1:8788:8788 \ -e ARTEX_PG_HOST=host.docker.internal \ -e ARTEX_PG_PORT=5432 \ -e ARTEX_PG_USER=artex \ -e ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD='yourpass' \ -e ARTEX_PG_DBNAME=artex \ -e ARTEX_PG_SSLMODE=disable \ -e ARTEX_JWT_KEY_DIR=/app/keys \ -v "$PWD/data:/app/data" \ -v "$PWD/keys:/app/keys" \ ghcr.io/baarai/artex:latest # → http://localhost:8787 (docker logs artex | grep "Setup token") ``` In `docker-compose.yml` and `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is passed to ARTEX as its own variable. The server percent-encodes it into the connection URL, so a password may contain `/`, `?`, `%`, `@`, `:` or spaces. In `.env`, quote a value that contains `#`, and write `$$` for a literal `$`. The `ARTEX_PG_*` variables take the password raw; quote it in a shell. The image includes a scanner toolchain (`nmap`, `nuclei`, `httpx`, `katana`, `ffuf`, `dalfox`, `sqlmap`, `ripgrep`, `curl`, `npm`, …) and built-in `/app/skills`. The GHCR Compose file below persists `./keys` and `./data`; it does not mount a host `skills/` directory, so the image's built-in skills are used. #### Compose stack from the prebuilt image `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` runs the same ARTEX + PostgreSQL stack from the released image, with no checkout build. The image is not published yet: v0.7.0 predates the GHCR publish step, so use the checkout build above until the next tagged release. Once the first image is published, download the file and `.env.example` once: ```bash curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/main/docker-compose.ghcr.yml curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/main/.env.example cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, optionally an LLM key docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml pull docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up -d # → http://localhost:8787 (docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml logs artex | grep "Setup token") ``` Update the stack without a git checkout: ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml pull docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up -d ``` Pin a version with `ARTEX_IMAGE_TAG=v0.7.1` in `.env` (or `0.7.1`); unset uses `latest`. To use custom skills, copy them into a host directory and add `- ./skills:/app/skills` to the `artex` volumes, which overrides the built-in `/app/skills`. For remote MCP you can choose `http` (Streamable HTTP) or `sse` (legacy SSE) in system settings. Legacy SSE servers usually establish the event stream with `GET /sse` and receive JSON-RPC over `/message?sessionId=...`; configure the URL as `/sse` and send `Authorization: Bearer `. ### Option 3: prebuilt binaries (Releases) Download the zip for your platform from [Releases](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases). It contains `artex`, `start.sh` (`start.bat` on Windows), `skills/` and `config.example.json`: ```bash cp config.example.json config.json # fill in the database connection ./start.sh # → http://localhost:8787 ``` Start with `start.sh` / `start.bat`, not `./artex`: it is a daemon script that restarts the process after a backoff. To keep it in the background: `nohup ./start.sh >artex.log 2>&1 &`. #### Verifying a release Each release attaches `SHA256SUMS` and a CycloneDX SBOM, `artex-.cdx.json` (Go modules in the linux/amd64 binary, the frontend `package-lock.json`, `go.mod`/`go.sum`), next to the zips. The zips also carry a GitHub build provenance attestation. Releases published before this was added have neither. ```bash sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS # add --ignore-missing if you downloaded only some zips gh attestation verify --repo BaaRai/ARTEX # built by this repository's release workflow ``` ### Option 4: build the single binary from source ```bash cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. cp -r web/out server/webui/dist CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex ./start.sh ``` Only `-tags embedui` embeds the frontend into the binary. ### Option 5: cross-platform release archives `build.sh` builds and embeds the frontend, strips debug info, and writes zips for Linux amd64/arm64, macOS amd64/arm64 and Windows amd64 by default: ```bash ./build.sh --release # output: dist/artex--*.zip ARTEX_TARGETS=linux/amd64,windows/amd64 ./build.sh --release ./build.sh --target linux/amd64 --upx ``` UPX is disabled by default: self-extracting binaries may be incompatible with some kernels, virtualization environments or security policies. Pass `--upx` only after confirming the target runtime supports it. --- ## Configuration **Database** (`config.json`, `ARTEX_PG_DSN`, or `ARTEX_PG_*` environment variables — see [External PostgreSQL](#external-postgresql)): ```json { "database": { "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 5432, "user": "artex", "password": "yourpass", "dbname": "artex", "sslmode": "disable" } } ``` **LLM**: `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`), or configure it in the UI's "LLM Configuration" page, which can also add a local Ollama server as a keyless provider (format "Ollama", default base URL `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`). Optional: `ARTEX_LLM_PROVIDER` (`anthropic | openai | openai-responses | ollama`), `ARTEX_LLM_MODEL`, `ARTEX_LLM_BASE_URL`, `ARTEX_LLM_PROXY`. **Base URL gotcha**: for the Anthropic format, enter the host **without** `/v1` (for example `https://api.anthropic.com`); ARTEX appends `/v1/messages`. OpenAI-format providers append `/chat/completions` (or `/responses` for `openai-responses`), so their base **does** end in `/v1` (for example `https://api.openai.com/v1`). **OpenAI-compatible gateways**: any provider that serves an OpenAI-style `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint works through the **OpenAI** format — no dedicated format needed. Create a profile with format **OpenAI**, set **Base URL** to the gateway's `/v1` root, paste the key, then click the **↻** button next to *Model* to load the provider's catalog (`GET /v1/models`) and pick a model; models the provider adds later appear on the next refresh. For example, [NotHoly](https://notholy.com) (offensive-security models) uses base URL `https://api.notholy.com/v1` with an API key from its console. **Task archive storage**: local disk by default. Set `ARTEX_ARCHIVE_STORAGE=s3` to store cold task packages in an S3-compatible bucket and release their local package space after verification. Existing local archives remain usable. See [Task archive storage](docs/task-archive-storage.md) for configuration, permissions, integrity checks, temporary disk requirements and recovery. **Concurrency**: work agents per task, in "System Settings" (default 3). **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results for the worker, planner, chat and main agent are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Unset or empty, the boundary is on; set `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0` (or `false` / `off` / `no`) to disable it. Cost: about 154 bytes per tool result plus one system note. **Noise profile (off by default)**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE` paces the requests ARTEX sends to targets (WebFetch, HTTP custom tools, the enrich probe). Unset or `off` keeps today's behaviour: no limit, no cache. `quiet` = 2 req/s per host (burst 4, 1 in flight), `balanced` = 5 req/s (burst 10, 2 in flight), `aggressive` = 20 req/s (burst 40, 4 in flight). A profile adds jitter, backs off on 429/503 (honours `Retry-After`, bounded retries, GET/HEAD/OPTIONS only), deduplicates identical in-flight GETs and caches them briefly (60/30/10 s; never POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), and logs a per-host noise line each minute. `ARTEX_TARGET_USER_AGENT` sets a User-Agent on target requests that carry none. With traffic capture on, Bash commands that use the proxy (curl, wget, python-requests) are paced too, per host by the same rate and jitter, and counted in the same per-host lines. The in-flight caps, retries and cache apply only to ARTEX's own requests. This is best effort, not a security boundary. Raw scanners such as nmap are not paced, and neither is a command that bypasses the proxy (`--noproxy`, a removed proxy variable). With capture off, nothing launched from Bash is paced. The low-and-slow prompt block supplies the rate flags in every case. The **Target noise** card in System settings sets the profile at runtime (no restart) and shows the per-host counters; once saved, that setting takes precedence over `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE`. **Low-and-slow agent guidance (off by default)**: when a noise profile is set, the planner, worker, main agent and chat agents receive a code-owned prompt block with the profile's per-host limits and exact rate/delay flags for the installed scanners. It tells them to test one host at a time, back off on 429/503 and never raise the rate to meet a deadline. **Run budgets (off by default)**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a task's total spend (planner rounds and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Unset or `0` means unlimited. A worker is not started when the remaining task budget cannot cover its estimated cost (the average of finished workers, else 50,000 tokens and 10 turns). Near the wrap-up reserve (the larger of 5% and 20,000 tokens, and 2 turns) the task enters a forced wrap-up: the planner writes a summary and final goal judgment, and workers may only write back. The task then ends `done` if its goals are met, else `timeout`. Practical floor: below 50,000 tokens no worker starts; 50,000-70,000 typically gives one worker then wrap-up; pick well above 70,000 for real exploration. Planner, worker, judge, and compactor rows in `llm_usage` are counted back into the cap when a ledger is created, including after a restart and after a revived run drops its ledger. A restored task already inside the wrap-up reserve does not get another worker: only that reserve remains, and the run wraps up. Chat, goal decomposition, and side questions are stored on the same task and are not counted. The per-worker average is not restored (usage rows have no run boundary), so the estimate starts from the defaults until a worker finishes in this process. **Common flags**: `./start.sh -addr :8787 -proxy :8788` (`-addr` frontend/API, `-proxy` traffic recording proxy). ### External PostgreSQL ARTEX already supports an external PostgreSQL 16+ instance — the `postgres` service in `docker-compose.yml` is only the bundled default. Because the database is startup configuration and the system's single source of truth, there is no runtime database switcher in the UI: change the environment variables and restart the server to point at another instance. Configure the connection with either a full connection string or individual parts: - **`ARTEX_PG_DSN`**: full PostgreSQL connection URL (for example `postgres://artex:pass@db.example.internal:5432/artex?sslmode=require`). When set, it takes precedence over the `ARTEX_PG_*` variables and you are responsible for percent-encoding any URL-special characters in the username or password. - **`ARTEX_PG_*` parts** (recommended when passwords contain `/`, `?`, `%`, `@`, `:`, or spaces — ARTEX percent-encodes the user and password and removes `ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD` from the environment at startup): - `ARTEX_PG_HOST` — PostgreSQL host - `ARTEX_PG_PORT` — PostgreSQL port (default `5432`) - `ARTEX_PG_USER` — database user - `ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD` — database password (raw, not URL-encoded) - `ARTEX_PG_DBNAME` — database name - `ARTEX_PG_SSLMODE` — TLS mode (`disable`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full`) #### Compose without the bundled `postgres` service To run ARTEX against an external PostgreSQL server with Docker Compose, remove the `postgres` service, the `depends_on` block, and the `pgdata` volume from `docker-compose.yml`, and point `artex` at your database: ```yaml services: artex: image: ghcr.io/baarai/artex:latest security_opt: - "no-new-privileges:true" environment: # Option A: individual parts (recommended; percent-encodes special characters) ARTEX_PG_HOST: ${ARTEX_PG_HOST:?Set ARTEX_PG_HOST in .env} ARTEX_PG_PORT: ${ARTEX_PG_PORT:-5432} ARTEX_PG_USER: ${ARTEX_PG_USER:-artex} ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD: ${ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD:?Set ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD in .env} ARTEX_PG_DBNAME: ${ARTEX_PG_DBNAME:-artex} ARTEX_PG_SSLMODE: ${ARTEX_PG_SSLMODE:-require} # Option B: full DSN (overrides ARTEX_PG_* when set) # ARTEX_PG_DSN: ${ARTEX_PG_DSN} ARTEX_JWT_KEY_DIR: /app/keys ports: - "${ARTEX_BIND_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}:8787:8787" - "127.0.0.1:8788:8788" volumes: - ./data:/app/data - ./keys:/app/keys restart: unless-stopped ``` #### Local disk usage (`data/`) Moving PostgreSQL to an external host does **not** move the runtime `data/` directory off local disk. `data/` still stores spilled HTTP/TCP traffic blobs (`data/traffic/_blobs`), LLM transcripts, task working files, and local task archives, so heavy workloads can still fill the host disk if `data/` is on a small volume. Mount `data/` on a suitably sized volume, and consider setting `ARTEX_ARCHIVE_STORAGE=s3` (see [Task archive storage](docs/task-archive-storage.md)) to offload cold task archives to object storage. ### Reverse proxy deployment (HTTPS / exposing only 443) The frontend, API and SSE stream share port 8787 (the binary listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default; the Docker container publishes on `127.0.0.1`), and the activity stream is same-origin by default, so **no `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` is needed**: expose 443 and keep 8787 internal. SSE keeps a long-lived connection with continuous pushes, so the proxy **must disable buffering**; otherwise the browser connects but never receives events. Nginx example: ```nginx server { listen 443 ssl; server_name your.domain.com; # ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key ... location / { # 512 MiB combined file limit plus 1 MiB of multipart metadata. client_max_body_size 513m; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; # SSE essentials: buffering off, long timeouts, HTTP/1.1 proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_read_timeout 3600s; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; } } ``` **Login rate limit behind a proxy**: login allows 10 attempts per minute per client IP. Behind a proxy every request comes from the proxy's address, so without further setup all users share one budget and an attacker who fails 10 logins blocks everyone, admin included, for up to 15 minutes. Keep the `X-Forwarded-For` line and set `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (comma-separated CIDRs, empty by default) to the address ARTEX sees the proxy connect from: - **nginx and ARTEX both on the host** (binary, `./start.sh`): the peer is `127.0.0.1`; start ARTEX with `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1/32`. - **nginx on the host, ARTEX in Docker** (`docker-compose.yml`): the connection reaches the container from the Docker bridge gateway (a `172.x` address), not from `127.0.0.1`. Find it with `docker network inspect artex_default --format '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'` (the network is `_default`), put `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=/32` in `.env`, then `docker compose up -d`. For a peer in that list, ARTEX reads `X-Forwarded-For` from the right and takes the first address that is not a trusted proxy; from any other peer the header is ignored. Trust only proxies you run: a trusted peer can claim any client address. > Only when SSE needs a different origin from the page (e.g. a dedicated subdomain) should you set > `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` **at build time** (it is baked into the static bundle during `next build`; > setting it at container runtime has no effect). --- ## Operations ### Troubleshooting an empty tool call In the task's session transcript, expand the affected tool call and compare **Command** and **Output**. The `UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT` markers identify the boundary around tool output. They are expected and should stay enabled while troubleshooting. - **Command shows `{}`.** The recorded tool input is an empty JSON object. For a tool that requires a command, this means its command argument was missing. Check which model and version produced the call. - **Command shows `(empty)` or `(failed to load)`.** The transcript has no input detail to display or could not fetch it. If the session record contains a command, include that discrepancy in a report. - **Output shows `[]`.** This is the recorded result body. Check the row's success or failure indicator and its input separately before drawing conclusions about what ran. For a recurring problem, share the ARTEX version or commit, the model and version, and a sanitized excerpt of the affected input and result. Remove credentials, target data, and other sensitive content before sharing. ### Backups `scripts/backup.sh` dumps the Postgres database (and optionally the data directory) with timestamped output and rotation: ```bash scripts/backup.sh --with-data # db dump + data/ archive, keep 14 scripts/backup.sh --keep 7 # db only, keep 7 ``` Restore into a running stack: ```bash gunzip -c backups/artex-db-.sql.gz | docker compose exec -T postgres \ psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" ``` Stored secrets (LLM API keys and proxies, MCP env, task credentials, notification channel config, Brave/Tavily search keys, web search and global proxies, the execution spec of custom tools, the capture-proxy rewrite rules) are encrypted in the database with the key in `keys/secret.key` (generated at first start, mode 0600, next to `jwt.key`). **A database backup without that key cannot restore those secrets**: back up `keys/` with the dump, separately. Deployments without a persistent disk set `ARTEX_SECRET_KEY` (32 bytes, base64 or hex, e.g. `openssl rand -base64 32`). ARTEX refuses to start when the database holds encrypted secrets and no key is available. Daily cron example (03:20, operator crontab): ``` 20 3 * * * cd /path/to/ARTEX && scripts/backup.sh --with-data >> backups/backup.log 2>&1 ``` ### Updating and upgrading > Upgrading swaps the program and never touches data: the Postgres volume `pgdata`, `./data` > (traffic index, task files, transcripts), `./keys` (`jwt.key`, `secret.key`) and `./skills` are > preserved. **No manual database step is needed**: on every start ARTEX applies its embedded > `schema.sql` baseline, then any pending numbered migration from `db/migrations/`, in order, each > in its own transaction. Restarting the new binary is the upgrade. Back up `./data`, `keys/` and > the database before upgrading. **Update banner (opt-in, off by default)**: start ARTEX with `ARTEX_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to ask the public GitHub releases API for the latest tag, at most once per 24 hours (cached in memory; a failed check is not retried within that window). When the release is newer, the web UI shows a dismissible strip linking to Releases. The request sends only `User-Agent: artex-update-check`. Unset, ARTEX makes no update request and shows no banner. #### Upgrading from a clone made before 2026-10-23 The repository history was rewritten that day to drop a personal email address from the commit metadata. A clone made before then cannot fast-forward, and `./update.sh` now stops instead of silently rebuilding stale code. Recover once, then upgrade normally: ```bash git stash # only if you have local changes git fetch origin git reset --hard origin/main git stash pop # only if you stashed ``` Your data is unaffected: `./data`, the `pgdata` volume and `./skills` are not part of git history. #### Option 1: one-click update script ```bash cd ARTEX ./update.sh ``` The script optionally `git pull`s, then offers **① Docker update** (`docker compose build artex` → `docker compose up -d artex`) or **② local build update** (rebuild the frontend static assets, then recompile `./artex`; restart the process for it to take effect). #### Option 2: Docker (Compose or GHCR image) ```bash cd ARTEX git pull docker compose build artex docker compose up -d artex docker image prune -f # optional ``` If running the prebuilt `ghcr.io/baarai/artex` container directly, pull the new tag (`docker pull ghcr.io/baarai/artex:latest` or a pinned `:v`) and recreate the container with the same `/app/data` and `/app/keys` mounts. If you run the prebuilt Compose stack, the update is: ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml pull docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up -d ``` #### Option 3: prebuilt binaries Download the new zip, stop the old process, overwrite `artex` and `skills/` (keep `config.json` and `data/`), then restart: ```bash cp -r /skills ./ && cp /artex ./ ./start.sh ``` #### Option 4: build from source ```bash git pull cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. cp -r web/out server/webui/dist CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex # restart ./start.sh ``` --- ## Development ```bash ./dev.sh # backend(:8787) + traffic proxy(:8788) + frontend next dev(:5173) → http://localhost:5173 ``` - Backend: `go run ./cmd/artex` (without `-tags embedui`, the frontend is not embedded) - Frontend: `cd web && npm run dev` (`/api` is reverse-proxied to the backend, with hot reload) - Tests: `go test ./...` - Reproduce all CI checks locally: `./scripts/verify.sh` (add `--full` for `-race` and the static web build) - Mock preview (no backend): `cd web && NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK=1 npm run dev` --- ## Architecture ARTEX is an **LLM multi-agent-driven autonomous penetration testing system**: a Go monolithic backend (with the Next.js UI embedded) + PostgreSQL. Agent capabilities come from the [`norma`](https://github.com/Autumn-27/norma) SDK (`agentcore` / `tool` / `permission` / `harness` / `memory` / `transcript`). At its core is the **dual-graph architecture**, plus two autonomy mechanisms: **process-level information exchange between workers** and the **planner's multi-round shared todolist**. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph FE["Frontend Next.js (go:embed embedded single binary)"] UI["Dashboard · Tasks · Assets · Coverage graph · Traffic · Workspace · System settings"] end subgraph SRV["server (Go net/http)"] API["REST /api/* JWT auth SSE"] ENG["engine scheduling loop"] MGR["Manager task/engine/store lifecycle"] end subgraph AG["agent (norma SDK)"] GO["goals goal decomposition + scope extraction"] PL["planner the planner (sole intent generator)"] WK["worker executor ×N"] MA["mainagent human-in-the-loop"] end subgraph DB["PostgreSQL"] AGRAPH["Asset graph assets / companies / task_scope"] EGRAPH["Exploration graph exploration_nodes / anchors / activity"] end subgraph SUB["Supporting subsystems"] PROXY["Traffic recording proxy MITM + CA tracing"] GUARD["guard / intercept tool approval gate"] ENR["enrich DNS / HTTP async enrichment"] EXT["MCP · skills · memory · report"] end UI -->|HTTP| API API --> MGR --> ENG ENG --> PL ENG --> WK API --> MA API --> GO PL --> DB WK --> DB MA --> DB GO --> DB WK -->|"Bash / HTTP fully traced"| PROXY WK --> GUARD WK --> ENR PL -.-> EXT WK -.-> EXT MA -.-> EXT ``` | Layer | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | **Frontend** | Next.js static export embedded via `go:embed`; tasks, assets, exploration and coverage graphs, traffic, human-in-the-loop chat | | **server** | `net/http` routing, JWT auth, SSE; `Manager` owns tasks, engines and DB stores | | **engine** | One `plannerLoop` + N worker goroutines per task; intent claiming, timeout/pause/drain | | **agent** | goals / planner / worker / mainagent; `ToolSet` exposes the dual graphs as LLM tools | | **db** | PostgreSQL persistence (pgx); embedded schema and numbered migrations applied at startup | | **Supporting** | Recording MITM proxy, approval gate, async enrichment, MCP/skills/memory/report | For the code-level map (execution flow, trust boundaries, decisions) see [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); for startup, configuration precedence, backup and key rotation see [docs/OPS.md](docs/OPS.md). --- ## Security Please report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub Security Advisories; see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Operational security properties: - **Secrets at rest**: LLM keys/proxies, MCP environment, task credentials, notification config, search keys, proxies, custom-tool execution specs, capture-proxy rewrite rules and traffic evidence snapshots are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using `keys/secret.key` (or `ARTEX_SECRET_KEY`). ARTEX refuses to start when encrypted data exists and no usable key is available. - **First-run claim**: `/setup` requires a one-time token printed at startup; the UI binds to `127.0.0.1` by default. - **Login protection**: 10 attempts per minute per client IP, with `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` for correct client attribution behind a reverse proxy. - **Untrusted tool output**: framed as data for every agent by default (prompt-injection boundary). - **Release integrity**: SHA-256 sums, CycloneDX SBOM and GitHub build provenance attestations for release archives. --- ## About this fork This repository is the English translation and continuation of ARTEX, originally by [Autumn-27](https://github.com/Autumn-27). The upstream repository is no longer public, so the link points to the author profile. Changes in this fork are tracked in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), under the same AGPL-3.0 license. --- ## References and prior art - [Cairn](https://github.com/oritera/Cairn) - Approval-details UI inspired by [AegisHook](https://github.com/RuoJi6/AegisHook) --- ## License and disclaimer ### Open source license This project is licensed under the **GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)**; see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for the full terms. Anyone may use, modify and distribute this project, but **derivative works must also be open-sourced under AGPL-3.0**; in particular, **if you modify this project and provide it to users over a network (for example as an online service), you must make the corresponding complete source code available to those users**. > **Important**: the open source license does not restrict how the software is used. The usage > restrictions and disclaimer below are additional terms from the maintainers. **ARTEX is an offensive-security tool. Use it only against systems you own, or that you are explicitly authorized to test (your own lab, your organization's assets, or a bug bounty / vulnerability disclosure program's targets within its published scope and rules of engagement). Any use without authorization violates these terms.** ### Permitted use - Read, learn and study this project's source code; - Run it against systems you own or in isolated lab environments; - Run it against authorized bug bounty / vulnerability disclosure targets, within their published scope and rules of engagement; - Academic research and code review. ### Prohibited actions - Scanning, probing, exploiting or attacking any website, online service or networked system without the explicit authorization of its owner; - Testing outside a program's published scope, or in violation of its rules of engagement; - Illegal intrusion, data theft, extortion, denial of service, or any destructive or criminal activity; - Any use that violates the laws and regulations of your country or region. ### Compliance responsibility Users must comply with all laws and regulations of their country or region regarding cybersecurity, data protection and computer crime. **All legal liability and consequences arising from the use of this tool are borne by the user.** ### Disclaimer This project is provided "as is", without any express or implied warranty. items.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.

VoiceStudio

AI voice studio. On your device.

Clone, design, dub, dictate, transcribe and narrate in 646 languages.

Runs on your laptop, desktop, servers, phone, tablets and more

Website · Download · Get started · Docs · VoiceStudio Pro · VoiceStudio Cloud

🇬🇧 English · 🇨🇳 简体中文 · 🇯🇵 日本語 · 🇰🇷 한국어 · 🇷🇺 Русский · 🇸🇦 العربية · 🇩🇪 Deutsch · 🇪🇸 Español · 🇫🇷 Français · 🇮🇳 हिन्दी
🇮🇩 Bahasa Indonesia · 🇮🇹 Italiano · 🇳🇱 Nederlands · 🇵🇱 Polski · 🇵🇹 Português · 🇹🇭 ไทย · 🇹🇷 Türkçe · 🇹🇼 繁體中文 · 🇺🇦 Українська · 🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt

Strategic sponsors    ·   Special sponsor 



Demo workspace · Default dark theme · Watch the HD tour

## What you can do

Voice cloning
Turn a clean reference recording into speech in a familiar voice.
Video dubbing
Translate and dub videos with speech timed to the original.

Voice design
Describe a voice in words and generate it.
Local models
Choose your engines and download only the models you need.
More screenshots

Workspace overview
Model packs
- **Dictate & transcribe** — A floating dictation widget and local transcription - **Narrate & batch** — Stories, audiobooks and queued jobs - **Connect & automate** — Local API, MCP, reusable recipes and watch folders Start with **VoiceStudio** (default, powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice), or pick from dozens of other engines in the Model Manager. See the [features & engine catalog](docs/feature-catalog.md).

## Pro and Cloud Everything above is free, runs on your own hardware and needs no account. Pro and Cloud are optional.
  VoiceStudio Pro

For paid client work across more than one machine.
  • A Commercial License for VoiceStudio's code in your client work, emailed to you
  • One user on up to 3 devices at once
  • Send jobs to your other GPUs while your projects stay local
  • New features and fixes first
Closed-source build, account required, 7-day full refund. The AGPL-3.0 app stays free, including commercial use under its terms. Neither licence covers model weights: the default OmniVoice weights are non-commercial (CC-BY-NC), so check each model's licence in the Model Manager before client work.

See Pro plans → 		  VoiceStudio Cloud

A hosted voice and dubbing API, coming soon. No GPU needed.
  • Speech, voice design and voice cloning with consent
  • Dubbing, transcription and audiobooks
  • Usage and credits by day or project
  • Long jobs that run on their own
Not available yet: join early access for free usage credits. The desktop app stays free and local.

Join Cloud early access →
## Platforms Experimental [Windows ROCm setup](docs/install/windows-rocm.md) supports selected RDNA 2 RX 6000 GPUs with targets `gfx1030`, `gfx1031` or `gfx1032`; RX 6500 XT (`gfx1034`) is excluded. GPU transcription uses a CTranslate2 build with native `gfx1031` kernels that this repository builds from upstream source and pins by hash, and setup checks actual GPU kernel execution. RX 6700 XT tests also cover native Torch speech generation and PyTorch Whisper. ROCm 10 faster-whisper uses a separate inference process to preserve safe CPU selection and fallback. Other cards and workloads retain the qualification limits in the guide. Performance presets validate changed engine selections in an offline child process before saving them, preserving fallback when an installed runtime fails. Choose your system, then expand an installation method. Native GGUF engines additionally support engine-specific Vulkan acceleration on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs ([OmniVoice](docs/engines/omnivoice-gguf.md#vulkan-acceleration), [CosyVoice](docs/engines/cosyvoice-gguf.md)). OmniVoice GGUF selects its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux. Vulkan discovery retries a stalled hidden probe with a native summary; Windows and Linux desktop builds fail rather than silently ship without their Vulkan module.
macOS · Homebrew · DMG · installer
**Stable · Apple Silicon**
macOS 13.3+ · Apple Silicon: local engines with Metal (MPS). ```sh brew tap debpalash/tap brew trust --cask debpalash/tap/voicestudio brew install --cask debpalash/tap/voicestudio ```
DMG Download the DMG for your Mac, open it and drag VoiceStudio into Applications. [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/macos.md)
One-command installer ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh ```
Intel Mac · remote backend · Limited The app UI runs on Intel; connect it to a VoiceStudio backend on another computer. [Guide](docs/install/macos.md)
> [!NOTE] > On macOS, "VoiceStudio is damaged and can't be opened" means Gatekeeper blocked the app, not that the download is broken. See the [Gatekeeper fix](docs/install/macos.md#gatekeeper-quarantine).
Windows · PowerShell · EXE
**Stable · x64**
Windows 10/11 x64 · NVIDIA CUDA · AMD ROCm (opt-in) · CPU. ```powershell irm https://voicestudio.sh/install.ps1 | iex ``` [Download the Windows installer](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/windows.md) · [AMD ROCm](docs/install/windows-rocm.md)
Windows on ARM · experimental Native app UI; the x64 Python backend runs under emulation on the CPU. [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/windows.md)
Linux · AUR · Snap · DEB · AppImage · Nix
**Stable · x64**
Linux x64 · NVIDIA CUDA · CPU · Vulkan for supported GGUF engines.
One-command installer ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh ```
Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS · AUR ```sh yay -S voicestudio-bin ``` Also available through `paru -S voicestudio-bin`. [Development sources](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/voicestudio-git) · `yay -S voicestudio-git`
Build from AUR and install with pacman ```sh sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel git git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/voicestudio-bin.git cd voicestudio-bin makepkg -s sudo pacman -U ./voicestudio-bin-*.pkg.tar.zst ```
Ubuntu / Debian / Linux Mint · DEB Download the `.deb` into the current folder, then install it: [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) ```sh sudo apt install ./VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.deb ```
Snap · Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE and more With [snapd installed](https://snapcraft.io/docs/installing-snapd): ```sh sudo snap install voicestudio ``` To enable microphone access: ```sh sudo snap connect voicestudio:audio-record ```
Any Linux distribution · AppImage Download the AppImage into the current folder, then launch it: [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) ```sh chmod +x VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.AppImage ./VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.AppImage ```
Nix / NixOS · source environment Enter the repository’s FHS development environment, then run from source: ```sh git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git cd VoiceStudio nix develop .#fhs bun run dev ``` [Guide](docs/install/nix.md)
[Guide](docs/install/linux.md)
Docker · GHCR · Docker Hub
Stable images · CPU · NVIDIA CUDA · AMD ROCm. **Run locally on the CPU (Bash)** ```sh export OMNIVOICE_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" docker run -d --name omnivoice \ -p 127.0.0.1:3900:3900 \ -e OMNIVOICE_API_KEY \ -e OMNIVOICE_DATA_DIR=/app/omnivoice_data \ -v omnivoice-data:/app/omnivoice_data \ ghcr.io/debpalash/voicestudio:stable printf 'API key: %s\n' "$OMNIVOICE_API_KEY" ``` Open http://localhost:3900 and use the API key printed below. [NVIDIA, AMD ROCm and Compose instructions](docs/install/docker.md) [Docker Hub mirror](https://hub.docker.com/r/palashdeb/omnivoice-studio): `palashdeb/omnivoice-studio:stable`
Android · APK · Obtainium · F-Droid repository
Android 10+ · Preview · On-device, offline after model download. [Download APK](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/mobile.md#install)
F-Droid · VoiceStudio repository Add this repository in an F-Droid-compatible client; verify the fingerprint in the guide. ```text https://debpalash.github.io/VoiceStudio/fdroid/repo ``` [Guide](store/fdroid/README.md)
Obtainium · GitHub releases Add this source in Obtainium, or import the provided configuration. ```text https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio ``` [Import configuration](https://debpalash.github.io/VoiceStudio/obtainium.json)
Install over USB with adb ```sh adb install -r VoiceStudio-*-android.apk ```
iPhone / iPad · IPA · sideloading
iOS / iPadOS 17+ · Preview · On-device, offline after model download. Download the IPA and follow the signing and sideloading instructions. [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/mobile.md#install)
Desktop and phone installers are on the [latest release](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest); Docker images come from GHCR. No GPU? The app is fully usable on the CPU, just slower. Native GGUF engines can also use Vulkan on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs; OmniVoice GGUF picks its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux ([OmniVoice](docs/engines/omnivoice-gguf.md#vulkan-acceleration), [CosyVoice](docs/engines/cosyvoice-gguf.md)). Speed by engine and hardware: [performance](docs/performance.md). ## Get started Install using the options above. Then open **Voice cloning**, pick a voice or add a clean reference recording, type your text and generate. The app asks before it downloads any model.
More install options: a specific version, current main, uninstall, from source, with a coding agent ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --version X.Y.Z # a specific release curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --main # build current main curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --uninstall # remove the app, keep your data ``` If `voicestudio.sh` is unreachable, run the script straight from the repository: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`. Prerequisites and behavior: [installer guide](docs/install/script.md). **From source** ```bash git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git cd VoiceStudio bun run dev ``` `bun run dev` installs the JavaScript dependencies and, when using a supported local backend, the Python dependencies before launching Electron. Run `bun run setup:api` directly when you only need to rebuild the Python environment. See [Electron setup](electron/README.md). **With a coding agent** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …), paste: ```text Install the VoiceStudio app on this device and verify it works, following https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/blob/main/docs/install/agent.md ``` Upgrading from 0.5.3 or older (the Tauri app)? [Install the new app separately](docs/electron-migration.md).
## Documentation [All guides](docs/README.md) | Need | Start here | |---|---| | Setup help | [Troubleshooting](docs/install/troubleshooting.md) · [Model downloads](docs/downloading-models.md) | | Guides | [Multi-speaker dubbing](docs/dubbing/multi-speaker-guide.md) · [Expressive speech](docs/expressive-speech.md) · [Exporting dubs](docs/dubbing/export.md) | | Models & quality | [Engine guides](docs/engines/README.md) · [whisper.cpp ASR](docs/engines/whisper-cpp.md) · [Benchmarks](docs/benchmarks.md) | | Integrations | [CLI](docs/install/script.md#terminal-command) · [Local API](docs/speech-platform.md) · [MCP](docs/mcp.md) · [Examples](examples/README.md) | | Phone apps | [iOS and Android](docs/mobile.md) | | Development | [Contributing](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) ([sign the CLA](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribution-licensing) before your first PR) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Code signing policy](docs/code-signing-policy.md) | Agent skills: `npx skills add debpalash/VoiceStudio` (**voicestudio** for audio work, **voicestudio-maintainer** for the repo). ## Sponsors The VoiceStudio app is free and needs no paid cloud. Sponsors keep it shipping: they fund maintainer time, test hardware, code-signing and release infrastructure.

For sponsorship inquiries, contact [sponsor@voicestudio.sh](mailto:sponsor@voicestudio.sh). items.description: 在 dsh 里装上这个插件即可，无需登录、注册或填 API Key，就能使用包括 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Kimi K3 在内的前沿模型——完全免费，不限量。 All you do is install this plugin in dsh: no login, no sign-up, no API key — the frontier models are just there, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Kimi K3 among them. Completely free, with no usage cap.
items.readme_text:
# dsh-our-free-model **简体中文** | [English](README_EN.md)

Trendshift JavaScript 周榜第 1 · 2026-10-05 至 2026-10-11 · 更新中，截至 2026-10-11
> 你只需在 dsh 里装上这个插件，无需登录、注册、填 API Key 或任何其它操作， > 就能用上包括 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Kimi K3 在内的前沿模型——完全免费，不限量。 > > *All you do is install this plugin in dsh: no login, no sign-up, no API key, nothing > else. The frontier models are just there — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and the rest. > Free, with no usage cap.* > > 模型清单跟随上游刷新，可用性由**你自己这台机器的网络出口**实测得出， > 思考强度下发的是真实预算而不是提示词，另附一个 OpenAI 兼容的本地转发端口。 > > 纯插件挂载：不改内核、无构建步骤、零依赖。
--- ## 交流群

QQ 群：386179533（OFM技术交流群[1群]）
扫码加入群聊，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。
--- ## 亮点 - **开箱即用，无配置环节**——不需要账号、不需要 Key、不需要在后台申请配额。 - **上游来源公开透明**——免费车道来源为 [OpenCode 的 Zen 网关](https://opencode.ai)，Kilo 渠道来源为 [Kilo AI 的公共网关](https://kilo.ai)，均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。 - **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。 - **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。 - **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。 - **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。 - **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。 - **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 `application/json` 的 content-type 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。插件按响应体形状判定，并将已嗅探的字节重新注入流，既不会导致整轮失败，也不会因 header 与实际内容不符而将可用模型判为不可用。 - **思考强度实际生效**——两类模型两种控制：声明了思考档位的模型（如 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、GLM 5.3 Flash）给出它自己的档位菜单（Off / Low / High / Max 等），选中值按原值下发到上游 `reasoning_effort`，上游会校验该字段、集合外的取值直接 400；没有档位菜单的模型（MiMo V2.6 等）走预算阶梯——Light / Balanced / Deep 对应输出 token 预算 2 048 / 8 192 / 模型上限，思考不可关闭的模型三档整体翻倍为 4 096 / 16 384 / 模型上限，因为思考与正文共享同一输出额度。两者都逐次调用留痕，设置页每张模型卡均标注档位或该档实际下发的上限（详见「思考强度：档位菜单与预算阶梯」）。 - **不依赖浏览器界面**——插件仅将 llm 作为硬依赖，在没有 web server 的 composition（如 dsh-tui）中同样完成启动并输出模型；看板模块挂载在独立的 fiber 上，待 webServer 就绪后再注册路由，因此既不会阻塞模型车道，也不会因插件先于 web 服务加载而永久丢失设置页。 - **用量看板，数据全部留在本机**——Token 热力图、总量曲线（支持总计与单模型视图）、输出速度与首字延迟逐次采样。不上传任何数据。 - **OpenAI 兼容转发端口**——本机其它工具通过 base URL 与 Key 即可调用这些模型。Chat 历史中 assistant 的字符串 `reasoning_content` 会随工具后续请求保留，包括显式空字符串；缺失字段不会被补造。 - **EAC 渠道（桌面端专属）**——在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端与 DSHEAC AIO 桌面端中自动解锁一条协付通道，模型以 EAC 前缀显示（如 EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash）；凭据加密密封，由宿主指纹闸门把守；该渠道在服务器侧校验 GitHub 授权（登录并 star 本仓库）后才放行对话；在命令行及其它宿主中该通道完全不存在。详见「EAC 渠道」。 - **Kilo 渠道（免密免费池）**——内置 Kilo AI 公共网关的免费模型池（`isFree` 清单实时拉取，含 `kilo-auto/free` 自动路由），无需任何账号或 Key；模型卡带 Kilo 徽章。思考强度与 EAC 渠道同款：模型自身的档位菜单（Off / Low / Medium / High，默认 High），经网关统一的 `reasoning` 参数真实下发——Off 已逐家族实测将思考归零（nemotron、ling、dots、poolside、apodex、cohere）；stepfun 与 liquid 端点强制思考（对关闭请求返回 400）、两个自动路由不透传关闭，这些模型的菜单不含 Off 档。该池由上游免费提供，上游会在其模型卡中声明 prompt 可能被记录用于改进服务——请勿发送敏感内容，详见「免责声明」。 - **聚合渠道，自带 Key**——设置页新增一页，把第三方端点接进同一条模型清单：注册表内置 76 家提供商（NVIDIA NIM、OpenRouter、Groq、Cerebras、SambaNova、Gemini、DeepSeek、Mistral、Together、Fireworks、SiliconFlow、Nebius、Chutes、Hugging Face、Cloudflare、Z.ai、Kimi、MiniMax、QwenCloud/Alibaba、Bedrock、Vertex、Vercel AI Gateway、Azure OpenAI、FleetRelay Gateway，以及无需账号的 Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp），写入 Key（本机免账号的提供商不需要）后其模型即以 `provider/model` 出现在选择器里，也可经本地网关调用。Key 只写入本机 0600 的 settings.json，API 只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹；每家可单独启停、测试（列表探测，不花一次生成）、发现模型、覆盖 Base URL 与模型清单。OAuth 与 ADC 认证的提供商照常列出，但标注为不可驱动。 - **省 Token**——三件事：工具输出压缩（RTK）在请求发出前就地重写 `tool_result`（git diff / status / log、grep、find、ls、tree、构建日志、编号转储、搜索清单、重复日志行），实测 40 KB 的 `git diff` 移除 90% 的字节且模型仍能就它作答；提示词瘦身有 caveman 与 ponytail 两族、默认全关；另有五个不占用上游请求的本地应答。设置页用与用量图表同一批统计行显示压缩前后字节、节省比例、压缩块数与统计调用数。 - **路由（降级链）**——把任意车道的模型串成一条命名链，以 `combo:` 作为虚拟模型出现在选择器与网关上；`fallback` 固定从链首开始，`round-robin` 轮换起点并连续 N 轮粘滞。链接在输出任何正文之前失败会被整段丢弃，切换对调用方不可见；思考增量不算正文，因此「想了很久才撞上配额墙」正是降级最有价值的场景。 - **本地网关原生说 Anthropic**——新增 `POST /v1/messages`（流式与非流式，含 thinking / tool_use 块、真实 stop_reason 与流内 error 事件）与 `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`（本地估算）；`/v1/models` 广播全部车道，含聚合行与链路。网关页新增「接入客户端」分区，按实际绑定的端口与真实要求的密钥生成 Claude Code、Codex、OpenAI SDK、Anthropic SDK、curl 与局域网的可复制配方。 - **接口具备鉴权围栏**——插件 HTTP 路由优先级高于内核 `/api`，因此内置与内核一致的信任检查（优先复用 composition 的 connection 服务，缺失时退回结构化围栏）。 - **十个账号渠道，一体接入**——LobsterAI（有道）、Qoder / Qoder 中国版（阿里系）、TRAE（字节）、Cline、Loomy（讯飞）、Raccoon（商汤）、MiniMax Code、ZCode（智谱）、Gemini（Google Code Assist）十个账号渠道开箱即用，外加 Kilo 免费车道与原匿名免费通道；OpenCode 账号渠道在本插件中默认停用。各渠道的登录流程、账号池、每日积分领取、模型黑名单与其本地 OpenAI 网关（Chat Completions + Responses，默认 `127.0.0.1:8326`）原样挂载与运行；凭据只写入宿主凭据库，浏览器永远拿不到明文。 - **视觉特效按需开启**——设置页顶部“视觉特效”开关默认关闭，鱼缸和业务功能始终保留；开启后恢复背景光晕、毛玻璃与装饰动画，选择仅保存在当前浏览器。 - **OFM 插件中心：渠道 / 增强 / 页面统一市场**——新仓库 [Ebony-Vinyl/ofm-extensions](https://github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/ofm-extensions) 承载社区插件：Ed25519 签名索引、安装即校验 SHA-256 与静态扫描、运行在 Worker VM 沙箱（唯一 import 是受控的 `ofm:sdk`，网络只放行 manifest 声明的域名，密钥只进不出，每个 hook 带超时熔断）。渠道插件装上即出现在模型选择器（支持 `replaces` 接管内置车道），增强插件以 `onRequest`/`onModels`/`onUsage` 挂进请求链；页面插件在侧边栏贡献一个沙箱 iframe 页面，只能通过受控消息桥读写自己的配置与存储。清单 v1 与 v2 双兼容；内置账号渠道包、聚合渠道目录、客户端启动器、资源库格式与模型工作台也以 built-in 描述符登记在同一插件中心，不可卸载但可查看贡献。发现、安装、更新、启停、配置、密钥、自检、卸载全部在控制台「插件中心」完成；开发者模式可安装本地未签名包（显式风险确认、未验证徽标、同一沙箱）。市场页另带封面横幅、类型色带与骨架屏，详情弹层含签名源码直达链接、发布说明（changelog）与权限清单；索引由宿主后台定时刷新，已装插件的清单可一键导出 / 分组下的任意模型。选择结果按会话持久化。 **调整思考强度**：同一菜单中的 Effort。声明了思考档位的模型给出它自己的档位（如 Off / Low / High / Max），选中值按原值下发；其余模型给 Light / Balanced / Deep 三档，档位越高思考占用的 输出预算越多，上限为强制下发，因此档位之间存在可测量的差异。思考与可见回答共享同一输出额度， 因此思考不可关闭的模型会将三档整体上移（设置 → Our Free Model 的模型卡上标注了每档的 实际数值，声明档位的模型则标注档位名）。若回答被截断，可切换至更高档，或调高设置中的 单次输出上限。 **供本机其它工具调用**：设置 → Our Free Model → 本地转发，启用后复制 base URL 并生成 Key。支持： - GET /v1/models - POST /v1/chat/completions（流式与非流式） - POST /v1/responses - POST /v1/messages（流式与非流式，Anthropic Messages） - POST /v1/messages/count_tokens（本地估算，插件不含 tokenizer） 端口被占用时插件不会静默失效：先在同一端口重试数轮（刚关闭的监听、刚删除的 portproxy 规则通常在数百毫秒内释放），仍被占用则顺延至下一个可用端口，并在设置页标注 "请求的 18899 不可用，实际监听 18900"，落盘的也是该实际端口。Windows 上最常见的占用 来源是一条 netsh interface portproxy 规则（由 IP Helper 服务承载）：其对 0.0.0.0 的 监听会导致回环绑定直接返回 EACCES（区别于 EADDRINUSE）。netsh interface portproxy show all 可列出规则，netsh interface portproxy reset 可清除规则。 转发端点为全流式：除 `data:` 帧外，思考期间的静默由周期性写出的 SSE 注释帧 （以 `:` 开头）填充，客户端的 idle 超时因此不会将"上游仍在推理"误判为"连接已断开"。思考内容按 reasoning、reasoning_content、reasoning_text 三个字段识别——同一段思考若被上游同时 写入两个字段只计一次——reasoning_details 数组同样识别。上游本身不流式输出思考的模型，此处 也不会产生思考帧，详见「已知边界」。 **供同一网络中的其它设备使用**：同一面板下方还提供"局域网访问"。该功能默认关闭；启用后中继绑定一个可路由地址（默认 0.0.0.0），并要求使用独立的局域网 Key——与上述本机 Key 互不通用，因此任一泄露只需轮换对应一侧，本机已配置的工具不受影响。中继将请求原样转发至本机监听，模型清单、流式行为与错误语义与本机完全一致。端口填 0 表示自动分配（本机 18899 常已被占用或被端口代理占用），启用后面板会显示实际端口与局域网地址。**局域网地址按本机网卡实时读取**：面板在开启期间每 15 / jitterRatio。将这三项嵌套在 backoff:{} 中， 调度器读到 undefined，于是 undefined \* 2ⁿ = NaN，而持久会话日志会直接拒绝非有限数值—— 一个本可恢复的瞬时故障因此导致整轮对话报废。应返回已解析完毕的扁平策略。 **一次被中断的工具调用会永久污染该会话。** 缺少对应结果的工具调用在重放时，上游返回 400 invalid_request_error，此后该会话中的每一次请求都会失败。本插件在发送前修复配对， 三种线协议共用同一处修复逻辑。 **未在 inject 中声明的服务，属性直读会抛错（与返回 undefined 不同）；而 ctx.get() 在服务 "尚未被 provide 出来"时返回 undefined。** 这两条本轮各自触发过一次问题：将 inject 缩减为仅剩 llm Σtoken / Σ秒，不再对各次速率取平均——曾有一个 1 ms 的窗口将 26 次调用的均值抬高了三个数量级。因此答案集中在一两个大帧中落地的模型， 不具备可测量的输出速度，该栏显示 —。 ## 长思考截断后的自动恢复（issue #12） 所有模型默认启用一次有界恢复，Chat Completions、Messages、Responses 三种上游协议 共用该行为。触发条件为：首段仅有非空思考、无正文且无工具调用，且上游在未发送正常 结束帧的情况下直接关闭流；或上游发送了正常 stop 收尾、但同样只有思考而无正文——宿主会将 此类「空停」回合判定为空响应，恢复流程会继续请求一次正文。以下情况不触发恢复：用户取消、 已输出正文或工具调用的正常结束、达到输出上限、明确的上游错误。 插件将已收到的思考作为检查点文本，与原始输入一起发起新请求，要求直接输出整理后的回答。 该机制基于检查点重新发起请求，与上游原生 resume 无关，也不会重放已显示的思考内容。恢复段禁用工具调用；已输出 正文或已开始调用工具的截断回合不执行恢复，以避免内容重复或工具重复执行。 为避免重复长思考，恢复提示要求结论优先、最多 800 词；此为提示层面的约束（非硬性 token 限制），模型可能不遵守。恢复属于降级回答，原始请求中的长篇或逐步分析可能被简化。 每个逻辑回合最多两次物理请求：原始请求加一次恢复。默认总时限 900 秒（15 分钟），恢复段最多 300 秒，且受剩余总时长约束；恢复输出上限 8192 tokens，并继续受用户与模型的上限 约束。首段已知的输出 tokens 会从原始预算中扣除，恢复预算不足 512 tokens 时不发起恢复。 检查点最多 131072 字符，且必须通过基于文本字节的保守上下文余量估算；该估算不计算图片 token，不等同于精确的 tokenizer 校验。超出限制即停止恢复，不会无限续接。恢复必须正常结束且 产生非空白正文方为成功；失败返回 STREAM_CUT，宿主不会将该回合整轮重发，用户取消 则保持 aborted / ABORTED。 可通过本机 settings.json 的 streamRecovery: false 关闭恢复；也可通过对象的 enabled 开关及数值限制收窄边界，数值只能低于或等于默认上限。默认不限制模型名单。 用量看板将物理请求与逻辑回合分开统计。上游请求数与请求失败数按实际发出的请求次数计数； 对话回合数、回合失败数与已恢复数按一次适配器调用的最终结果计数。例如首段中断、 续写成功会记为 2 次上游请求、1 次请求失败，同时记为 1 个对话回合、0 次回合失败、 1 次已恢复。每段样本仍包含恢复关联、段序号与 noUsage 等标记；通过 recoveryId 关联各段的 noUsage 以判断缺失情况。最终上报宿主的 usage 仅汇总上游实际报告的已知值； 缺少某段 usage 时，该值不等于整轮完整 token 总量。思考检查点不写入统计文件。 升级前的旧统计仅包含物理请求记录，迁移后展示的回合数与失败数为基于这些记录的推算值， 看板会明确标注；升级后的回合按最终结果精确记录。 请求数、回合数与 Token 总量为累计值；速度、首帧延迟与热力图使用本机保留的历史窗口。 已在一次真实 MiMo V2.6 Flash · Deep 请求中恢复成功；此前一次恢复曾在 480 秒 截止时失败。这不代表全部模型均已实测，也不保证每个长思考回合都能生成答案。 下一节列出的 v1.3.1 记录描述的是恢复功能引入前的行为。 ## 验收情况 在 Windows 环境下针对真实上游实测。本节按轮次记录，并注明每项的验证方式——仅标注 「真实上游」与「实机点击」的条目才对应用户在界面上可见的行为。 ### Issue #12：验收状态 恢复实现、离线回归与真实上游结果单独记录在 session-map.json），并发的不同对话各自持有独立会话，互不共享上游状态。没有携带会话 id 的回合（部分宿主调用形态、本地网关未给出 user/conversation 的请求）会并入一枚保留的 global 会话，与其它无 id 回合共享上游状态（含 KV 缓存）——并行运行多个敏感对话时，请使用带会话 id 的调用形态；插件对首个无 id cookie/token）；不含 connection 服务的极简 composition 退回结构化围栏（loopback + 同源检查），本机其它进程仍可访问——与内核在同类 composition 下的行为一致。该说明同样适用于 /forward/key 与 /forward/lan/key：在这类 composition 下，本机任意进程通过一次请求即可取得转发 Key 与局域网 Key，再从其它机器消耗本机的免费额度。使用这类 composition 时，这两把 Key 应视作本机进程可读文件（与 settings.json 同一信任级别），如需更强隔离请在部署时挂载 connection 服务。 ## 开发 ``` npm test # 以下全部离线套件 + 清单一致性检查，一条命令 node scripts/client-lint.mjs # 除免费车道外，插件内置一条协付渠道（EAC）。宿主识别支持以下运行方式： DSHEAC AIO（Tauri 壳）：内核路径、内嵌 node、web-desktop profile 三重信号同时命中才解锁； DeepSeek Harness 桌面端（Electron 壳）与 DSH Tauri：使用内核提供的 `desktop` 或 `tauri` profile 上下文；仅有命令行参数不作为通过依据。 内核声明的 `web` / `web-desktop` profile 同样支持该渠道。未通过宿主识别时，不展示渠道、不发请求；通过识别后仍需满足独立的 GitHub 授权要求。 显示规则：模型名仅显示模型本名并带渠道前缀，如 EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、EAC Kimi K3；设置页的模型卡上另有独立的 EAC 渠道徽章。 加密密封：渠道凭据与端点从不以可读形式出现在插件中——它们仅以 AES-256-GCM 密文存在，解密密钥由分散在两个文件中的三片掩码分片在解锁时即时派生；非授权宿主不进入派生路径，密文对搜索引擎与字符串扫描而言仅为噪声。 凭据不落盘、不出进程：解锁按请求即时发生，明文仅存在于构造请求的那一帧中，不写入文件、不进入日志、不出现在任何 API 响应或错误消息中。 签名网关（推荐形态）：worker/ 目录附带一个 Cloudflare Worker 网关——插件密封的仅有网关地址与 HMAC 签名密钥，请求按 时间戳 + HMAC-SHA256(方法/路径/ body 摘要) 签名，中继的真实 key 仅存放于 Worker 的环境变量中；防重放时间窗、模型白名单、可选按 IP 限速均在网关执行，签名密钥泄露只需在网关侧轮换即可全体吊销。部署与轮换见 worker/README.md。 同样不会启动监听）——该端口的流量消耗的是本机这条免密车道，不应由一个字符串决定是否向整个子网开放。 局域网访问是另开的一扇门，并不放宽上述规则：本机监听仍只绑回环、修改地址仍被拒绝；需要跨机器使用时必须显式启用"局域网访问"，中继绑定可路由地址，且每个请求都需携带局域网 Key——连 /、/health 这类存活探针也一并鉴权（仅本机监听免 Key Key 互不通用；携带跳数标记的请求直接拒绝（508），因此端口即使配置为本机监听的同一端口也不会自环。局域网 Key 同样由 crypto 生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于同一 0600 文件中，可在面板上单独轮换。 转发 Key 由 crypto 运行时生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于 0600 权限文件中。本仓库不含任何硬编码凭据。/ 与 /health 为存活探针，先于 Key 检查应答，但仅回答"是否在线"，获取模型清单仍需 Key。 插件的 HTTP 路由带请求信任围栏（自 v1.1 修复）：插件的 /api/our-free-model 前缀在 webServer 的最长前缀分发下优先于内核 /api，曾绕过内核鉴权。当前每个请求先经由 composition 的 connection 服务准入（与内核 /api 完全同级的 cookie/token 校验）；connection 缺失的 composition 退回结构化围栏——loopback Host、拒绝跨站 sec-fetch-site、Origin/Referer 必须与 Host 同源同端口，Host 缺失或为空也拒绝（fail closed，不回退至 socket 本地地址）。实测结果：异源 Host/Origin 返回 403，无 cookie 的回环请求返回 401。connection 为逐请求获取，因为浏览器半身要到插件加载之后才将其 provide 出来——若在 apply 时以快照方式读取一次，围栏会在整个进程周期内退化为结构化那一层（本轮将该读取改回快照后，picker-test 的 401 断言立即失败）。 公告 HTML 在客户端经严格白名单渲染：scripts/sanitize-test.mjs 使用 XSS 语料（脚本注入、事件属性、javascript:/data: URL、iframe/svg/form、样式注入、畸形标签）验证全部被丢弃；不经过任何 innerHTML sink。公告源的 feedUrl 可被用户指向任意 URL，因此渲染器按不可信输入处理。 应用内升级的完整性链（v1.3.2 加签）：清单 Ed25519 签名验证（公钥 pin 在 src/updater.js，无签名或验签失败的清单直接拒绝，未签名镜像不会被安装）→ 清单校验（semver、路径逃逸、哈希格式、base 必须为清单相对路径）→ 下载时逐文件校验 SHA-256 与字节数 → staging 回读校验 → 安装后回读校验 → 任一步失败即恢复备份；安装前强制重新拉取清单，杜绝陈旧清单。文件与代码边界见已知边界一节。 更新通道与 feedUrl 彻底解耦（v1.3.2）：feedUrl 仅重定向公告 feed，永不再重定向升级清单——此前一个设置项即可将升级源指向任意服务器并配以自配平的哈希，等同于将"修改一个设置值"升级为"在宿主进程中执行任意代码"。公告 override 本身也收紧为仅 https（回环 http 除外，本机镜像与测试仍可用）且不得内嵌凭据。目标域不受限制：任何 https 地址均可作为 feedUrl，插件按 feedPollMinutes 的间隔轮询——因此在不含 connection 服务的 composition 中（见上文鉴权说明），能够修改设置的本机调用者可让进程持续请求任意外部地址。这与插件的其余外联一样按"设置即信任"对待：能够修改 settings.json 的人本来就能安装代码。 转发监听仅绑回环地址，且按解析结果绑定（v1.3.2）：localhost 这类主机名先经
